fixes.explanation: Divided is a fair guess, baker, but it's not Paul's worry here. The word he uses is conceited. That's a puffed-up head, like a cookie that rose way too big in the oven. Nothing in this verse mentions the church splitting up. Paul gives them the mystery so they won't be that.

Yes, baker. The Scripture goes on, “And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins.” Notice the when. The covenant is tied to God taking their sins away. That line runs right on from the Deliverer coming from Zion (Romans 11:26).

This one is actually true, so it's easy to trip on. The quote continues, “And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins.” So the covenant comes with God taking away their sins. That line runs right on from the Deliverer coming from Zion (Romans 11:26).

Kings are a natural guess, but Paul doesn't reach for them here. The name he gives is the patriarchs. Regarding election, Israel is loved on their account. Right beside that, he says regarding the gospel they are enemies on the Gentiles' account.

That's right. Paul says they too have now disobeyed, “…in order that they too may now receive mercy through the mercy shown to you.” It goes both ways. Mercy came to the Gentiles through Israel's disobedience (Romans 11:30), and now Israel may receive mercy through the mercy shown to the Gentiles.
Prophets are a natural guess, but Paul doesn't say mercy comes through their prayers. He says Israel may now receive mercy through the mercy shown to the Gentiles. That's the loop he describes.

That's right. Paul asks, “Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?” (Romans 11:35). It expects the answer no one, so there's no one God owes. Paul follows it with, “For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things.”
